question.text: Given that $r=-2\cot\theta$ for $\theta = \theta(t),$ and that$\dfrac{\textrm d r}{\textrm d t}=3$ at the point where $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{6},$ find $\dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t}.$
question.explanation:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

\begin{align} r &= -2\cot\theta \\[5pt] \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d t} (r) &= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d t} (-2\cot\theta) \\[5pt] \dfrac{\textrm dr}{\textrm d t} &= \dfrac{\textrm d\theta}{\textrm d t} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d \theta} (-2\cot\theta) \\[5pt] \dfrac{\textrm dr}{\textrm d t} &= \dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t} \cdot (2\csc^2\theta). \end{align}

Now we can substitute the given information $\dfrac{\textrm d r}{\textrm d t}=3$ and $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{6},$ and solve for $\dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t}.$ We get

\begin{align} \dfrac{\textrm dr}{\textrm d t} &= \dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t} \cdot 2\csc^2\theta\\[5pt] 3 &= \dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t} \cdot \left(2\csc^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right) \\[5pt] 3 &= \dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t} \cdot \left(2 \cdot 4\right) \\[5pt] \dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t} &= \dfrac 3 {8}. \\[5pt] \end{align}

question.text: A particle $P$ is moving along the curve $y=7x^3+5x$ such that the $x$-coordinate of $P$ is changing at the rate of $3 \,\textrm{m}/\textrm{h}.$ Find the rate of change of the $y$-coordinate when $x=1\,\textrm{m}.$
question.explanation:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

\begin{align} y&=7x^3+5x \\ \dfrac{\textrm d }{\textrm d t} (y)&= \dfrac{\textrm d }{\textrm d t}(7x^3+5x) \\[5pt] \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d t} &= \dfrac{\textrm d x}{\textrm d t} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d }{\textrm d x} (7x^3+5x) \\[5pt] \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d t} &= \dfrac{\textrm d x}{\textrm d t} \cdot (21x^2+5). \end{align}

Now, we can substitute the given information $\dfrac{\textrm d x}{\textrm d t}=3\,\textrm{m}/\textrm{h}$ and $x=1$ and get

\begin{align} \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d t} &= 3 \cdot (21\cdot 1^2 +5) \,\textrm{m}/\textrm{h} \\ &= 78 \,\textrm{m}/\textrm{h}. \end{align}

question.text: Given that $r=\tan{\theta} + 2\cot{\theta}$ for $\theta = \theta(t),$ and that $\dfrac{\textrm d r}{\textrm d t}=-\dfrac{1}{3}$ at the point where $\theta=\dfrac{2\pi}{3},$ evaluate $\dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t}$ at that point.
question.explanation:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

\begin{align} r &= \tan{\theta} + 2\cot{\theta} \\[5pt] \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d t} (r) &= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d t} \!\left( \tan{\theta} + 2\cot{\theta} \right) \\[5pt] \dfrac{\textrm dr}{\textrm d t} &= \dfrac{\textrm d\theta}{\textrm d t} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d \theta} \!\left( \tan{\theta} + 2\cot{\theta} \right) \\[5pt] \dfrac{\textrm dr}{\textrm d t} &= \dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t} \cdot \left( \sec^{2}{\theta} - 2\csc^{2}{\theta} \right). \end{align}

Now we can substitute the given information $\dfrac{\textrm d r}{\textrm d t}=-\dfrac{1}{3}$ and $\theta=\dfrac{2\pi}{3},$ and solve for $\dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t}.$ We get

\begin{align} -\dfrac{1}{3} &= \dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t}\cdot\left[\sec^{2}{\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)} - 2\csc^{2}{\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}\right] \\[5pt] -\dfrac{1}{3} &= \dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t}\cdot\left(4 - \dfrac{8}{3}\right) \\[5pt] -\dfrac{1}{3} &= \dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t}\cdot \dfrac{4}{3} \\[5pt] \dfrac{\textrm d\theta}{\textrm d t} &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-\dfrac{1}{4}}. \end{align}
